title: Influence bound for leading-coordinate majority
statement: Let $m$ be a natural number and let $\varepsilon,\delta\in\mathbb R$ with $0<\delta<1$. If every coordinate of the real-valued function obtained by multiplying odd majority on $2m+1$ signs by a new leading coordinate has stable influence at parameter $1-\delta$ at most $\varepsilon$, then $1-\sqrt{\delta}\leq\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: Every coordinate's stable influence at parameter $1-\delta$ is at most $\varepsilon$ for the real-valued leading-coordinate-times-majority function
